clue.text: Discharging account before leaving

indicators.note: in a down clue 'before' places the first piece above, so it is written earlier

blocks.note: AC is the standard abbreviation for account
quitting a place means leaving it

explanation.surface: Someone settles a bill just before walking out.
explanation.walkthrough: Discharging here is the legal sense: a court acquits, or discharges, a defendant.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquit someone is to release them from a charge, the legal sense of discharging a prisoner.

clue.text: Kisses people who punish children?

blocks.note: first meaning: slang for loud, hearty kisses
second meaning: those who smack, read literally as smack plus -ers

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is a whimsical coinage, which the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: Smackers is informal British slang for big noisy kisses, and also literally names anyone who smacks.

clue.text: Look, £1,000 on an old weapon

blocks.note: a grand is a thousand pounds, abbreviated G
a lance is a long spear carried by mounted knights

explanation.surface: Someone points out a thousand pounds paid for an antique weapon at auction.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means sits above, so the thousand comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A glance is a quick look, so the noun matches the noun.

clue.text: Stop giving support

blocks.note: first meaning: halt or remain
second meaning: a prop or brace, such as a ship's mast rope or corset bone

explanation.definitionFit: A stay halts proceedings, and a stay is also a rope or strut that braces something upright.

clue.text: Entrance being badly made, it can't

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the following letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the three words taken letter for letter, punctuation ignored

explanation.surface: A grand entrance flops: the performer simply couldn't pull it off.
explanation.definitionFit: Admittance is the right of entry, the same thing as entrance in the sense of getting in.

clue.text: Father and mother accepting Nora's view

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the parent words wrap around the name

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
ma is an informal word for mother
the woman's name taken as written; the possessive just builds the surface

explanation.surface: Nora's parents come round to sharing her opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: Father and mother join first, then take the name between them; 'view' looks like an opinion but is a scenic vista.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a wide unbroken view of a landscape, a synonym of view as scenery.

clue.text: Former union veto is thrown out

indicators.note: something thrown out is cast about and disordered, so the letters before it get rearranged

blocks.note: both words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A trade union's veto is rejected by its members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests a trade union, but the definition is the old Union of Soviet Socialist Republics.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet Union was the federation of communist republics dissolved in 1991, so it is a former union.

clue.text: Hitch horse behind pole

indicators.note: behind means placed after, so the animal follows the pole in the reading order

blocks.note: S is the south pole, one of the compass points
a nag is an old or worn-out horse

explanation.surface: Someone ties a horse up behind a post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hitch' looks like tethering a horse, but here it is a noun meaning a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is an unexpected difficulty or obstacle, which is what a hitch means as a noun.

clue.text: About fifty took part in the race and finished

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so the race phrase goes around the number

blocks.note: to take part in a race is to compete
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Around fifty runners entered the race and all reached the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Completed and finished are synonyms, both past tenses for bringing a task to its end.

clue.text: A party with sailors on deck

blocks.note: taken as written
a do is an informal word for a party
RN is the Royal Navy, the British fleet

explanation.surface: Sailors hold a party up on the ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' looks like part of a ship, but it is the verb meaning to decorate, as in deck the halls.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck something is to decorate or ornament it, the same as adorning it.

clue.text: Weird as a Parisian and shrewd!

blocks.note: un is the French word for a, as a Parisian would say it
canny means shrewd or astute

explanation.surface: A Parisian is called both strange and sharp-witted.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncanny means strange in an unsettling way, a close synonym of eerie or weird.

clue.text: Getting on with some pressing work?

definitions.text: Getting on with some pressing work?

blocks.clueFragment: Getting on with some pressing work?
blocks.note: surface reading: making progress on an urgent job
setter's reading: pressing literally, smoothing clothes with a hot appliance

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressing' looks like urgent, but it means flattening creases out of laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoothing clothes with a hot iron is literally pressing them, a household chore.

clue.text: Subject of article by crossword compiler

blocks.note: the is the definite article
the setter refers to themself as me; 'by' just places it next

explanation.surface: The topic of a piece written by the puzzle setter.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the main topic of a talk or piece of writing, a synonym of subject.

clue.text: Catch Rita renovating and cleansing

indicators.note: renovating means rebuilding and remodelling, so the preceding letters are rearranged

blocks.note: both words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone finds Rita doing up and scrubbing out her house.
explanation.definitionFit: Cathartic describes emotional release or purging, from the Greek word for purification, so it means cleansing.

clue.text: Delegated authority of apprentice chef is no different

indicators.note: made different means altered, so the two short words are reshuffled

blocks.note: a commis is a junior chef in a professional kitchen
both words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A trainee cook is said to have just the same powers as everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: A commis chef is the lowest rank in a restaurant kitchen brigade.
explanation.definitionFit: A commission is authority entrusted to someone to act for another, such as an agent or officer.

clue.text: Classes an accountant, for example, amongst politicians

indicators.note: to be amongst others is to sit inside the group, so the short abbreviation goes within the party

blocks.note: CA is a chartered accountant
Tories are members of the British Conservative Party
eg is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: An accountant sitting among MPs is offered as an example of social class.
explanation.walkthrough: CA stays outside; only the example goes inside the politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Categories are groups sharing characteristics, the same as classes in a classification.

clue.text: Musician wants what he plays on a table

blocks.note: a musician plays an instrument
taken as written
a table of data is a list

explanation.surface: A musician wants to rest his instrument on a table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Table' looks like furniture, but it is a list or chart.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrumentalist is a musician who plays an instrument rather than singing.

clue.text: Control liquid glue in class

indicators.note: something liquid flows and has no fixed shape, so the adhesive word's letters move around
in means placed inside, so the jumbled letters go within the word for class

blocks.note: taken as written, then jumbled
a rate is a grade or class, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: A teacher has to keep runny glue in the classroom under control.
explanation.definitionFit: To regulate is to control or govern by rules, a synonym of control as a verb.

clue.text: Girl with Holyhead fellow -- from Dublin?

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase standing for 'one from Dublin', a noun

blocks.note: Iris is a girl's name
read as the head of holy: its first letter
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A girl travels with a man from Holyhead, the Welsh ferry port for Dublin.
explanation.walkthrough: Holyhead is the Welsh port for ferries to Dublin, so the surface hangs together; split it into Holy plus head. The question mark marks Dublin as only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Dublin is an example of a native of Ireland, whose capital it is.

clue.text: Solidify and set fire to explosive material

blocks.note: to gel is to set into a jelly-like solid
to ignite is to set alight

explanation.surface: Instructions for setting something and then lighting a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelignite is a high explosive made from nitroglycerine in a gel, used in blasting.

clue.text: Glum Beryl hides some disused articles

indicators.note: hiding some of something means part of it is tucked inside the following words

blocks.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A gloomy Beryl stashes away some old junk.
explanation.walkthrough: In British use lumber is old furniture and junk, not timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumber in British English means unused furniture and odds and ends stored away, as in a lumber room.

clue.text: The support one member will need after the break?

definitions.text: The support one member will need after the break?

blocks.clueFragment: The support one member will need after the break?
blocks.note: surface reading: a club member needing backing after a holiday or pause
setter's reading: a member is a limb, and the break is a fracture of an arm

explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' means an arm and 'break' a fractured bone.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth support hung from the neck holds a broken arm still while it heals.

clue.text: I'd turned up lots before showing little emotion

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read from the bottom upwards
before places the second piece ahead of the first in the answer

blocks.note: the word lots, reversed
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone shows up with plenty but stays impassive.
explanation.definitionFit: A stolid person is calm and unexcitable, showing little feeling.

clue.text: Missing the first step, trips and falls over

indicators.note: missing the first step means the opening is lost, so the initial letter is dropped

blocks.note: to stumble is to trip

explanation.surface: Someone misses the bottom step, trips and goes flying.
explanation.definitionFit: To tumble is to fall headlong or roll over, so tumbles means falls over.

clue.text: Time to enquire after job

indicators.note: after means coming later, so the verb follows the abbreviation

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to enquire is to ask

explanation.surface: It is time to ask about a vacancy.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of work to be done, a synonym of job.

clue.text: Union man got ringleader into trouble

indicators.note: put into something means placed inside it, so the letter goes within the word for trouble

blocks.note: bother is trouble or fuss
read as the leader of ring: its first letter

explanation.surface: A trade unionist landed the strike's organiser in hot water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringleader' must be split into ring plus leader. Trade unionists address each other as brother.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a trade union traditionally call each other brother, so a union man is a brother.

clue.text: Former US president takes public transport to hospital

blocks.note: a bus is public transport
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: An ex-president rides the bus to hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bush, father and son, were both US presidents, now former holders of the office.

clue.text: Group in which we included "pudding"

indicators.note: in which describes a thing that holds something else inside it
included means taken inside, reinforcing that one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a set is a group
taken as written

explanation.surface: A club where members wrote 'pudding' into the minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain sweet is an everyday word for the dessert course.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet is British for the dessert course, the same as pudding in that sense.

clue.text: Stubborn stain to be shifted

indicators.note: shifted means moved about, so the letters before it change places

blocks.note: the three words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A stubborn mark that will need to be scrubbed away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stubborn stain' reads as one phrase, but stubborn alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstinate means refusing to change one's mind, a synonym of stubborn.
